simple.meaning: זַעַף (zaʻaph) is a Hebrew action word meaning “anger.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in 2 Chronicles, Proverbs, Isaiah, Jonah, Micah, beginning at 2 Chronicles 16:10. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, kingship, prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זַעַף (H2197) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: זַעַף (zaʻaph) / H2197 is traced through 2 Chronicles 16:10, 2 Chronicles 28:9, Proverbs 19:12, Isaiah 30:30 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2197. zaaph זַ֫עַף noun masculine storming, raging, rage (in poetry and late) — ׳ז absolute 2Chr 16:10 ; 28:9 ; construct Isa 30:30 2 t.; suffix זַעְמּוֺ Jonah 1:15 ; — 1 rage of king, leading to violence Prov 19:12 (|| כַּכְּפִיר נַהַם ), 2Chr 16:10 ( ׳בְּ עַלזֿאת עִמּוֺ ; || כעס ), 28:9 ; ׳ז אַף Isa 30:30 raging of anger (of ׳י ); ׳ז ׳י Micah 7:9 . 2 raging of sea Jonah 1:15 .

occurrences.englishText: Then Asa was angry with the seer, and put him in the prison; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. Asa oppressed some of the people at the same time.

But a prophet of Yahweh was there, whose name was Oded; and he went out to meet the army that came to Samaria, and said to them, “Behold, because Yahweh, the God of your fathers, was angry with Judah, he has delivered them into your hand, and you have slain them in a rage which has reached up to heaven.
The king’s wrath is like the roaring of a lion,
Yahweh will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, storm, and hailstones.
So they took up Jonah, and threw him into the sea; and the sea ceased its raging.
I will bear the indignation of Yahweh,
